title: NJ Clean Energy Program 2026: Comfort Partners, Charge Up, Solar Credits
desc: What New Jersey's Clean Energy Program offers homeowners in 2026: free Comfort Partners upgrades, Charge Up electric car incentives of $1,500 to $4,000, solar credits and net metering.
h1: New Jersey Clean Energy Program for Homeowners
badge: Free upgrades and up to $4,000 for an electric car
lead: New Jersey's Clean Energy Program is run by the state's Board of Public Utilities. It does not replace your utility's rebates. It adds free upgrades for lower incomes, cash toward an electric car, credits for solar owners, and rules that protect the value of your solar. These are the figures from the state's own site, read on October 6, 2026.
cards_intro: The state says funds are limited for some of these programs. Each card names the fact with the date and source link.

cards.title: Comfort Partners
cards.note: For households at or below 250% of the federal poverty level, or on TANF, Section 8, SNAP, SSI or General Assistance. Insulation, air sealing, a thermostat, efficient refrigerators and more. Call 866-378-4345.

cards.title: Charge Up New Jersey
cards.note: $1,500 for a new electric car at an eligible dealer, $4,000 with Charge Up+ for income-qualified buyers, and up to $250 for a Level 2 home charger. Projected to run through June 2027.

cards.title: Successor Solar Incentive
cards.note: Credits on the power your rooftop system makes, for registrations from July 27, 2026.

cards.title: Net metering
cards.note: Full retail credit over a 12-month cycle for power you send out.

cards.title: Garden State Energy Storage Program
cards.note: A plan with options for home batteries, with no amounts or start date.

cards.title: Federal home energy rebates
cards.note: We found no New Jersey launch date or amounts for the federal-funded HOMES and HEAR rebates.

sections: How the state fits with your utility

Your electric company's rebates (PSE&G, JCP&L or Atlantic City Electric) pay for equipment such as heat pumps and appliances. The state pays for different things: free work for lower incomes, electric car incentives and solar. You can use both. For example, a lower-income household can get Comfort Partners work and then use the utility's heat pump rebate.

The home must be your primary residence and you must be the ratepayer of record with a participating electric or gas utility. The building can have up to 14 individually metered units, so many apartments and townhomes qualify, and buildings above 14 units do not. If you heat with oil, propane or kerosene, the page sends you to the state's Office of Weatherization at 800-510-3102. The income limit is $39,900 a year for one person, $82,500 for four and $139,300 for eight.

The solar credits apply to net-metered projects registered by a contractor through the state's portal. The residential block is 300 megawatts for Energy Year 2027, and registrations close when it is full or on June 1, 2027. Net metering credits you at the retail rate over 12 months. If you switch suppliers or change your anniversary date, the balance is credited at the lower wholesale price and a new cycle starts. See our solar guide for an example.

The federal 25C and 25D credits ended after 2025. The state's own federal-funded home rebates, called HOMES and HEAR, appear on a state page as a design only. We found no launch, so we do not state any amounts. The state is also planning a battery program, but it is still a proposal.
claim_heading: How to use the state programs
claim_steps: Check your income against the Comfort Partners table, and call 866-378-4345 if you qualify.
For an electric car, apply for Charge Up+ before you buy or lease.
For solar, ask your contractor to register the project with the state portal.
Keep proof of income and benefits ready.
Use your utility's rebates for equipment at the same time.

faq: Who runs the New Jersey Clean Energy Program?
The state Board of Public Utilities, which works with the electric and gas utilities.
A free program for households at or below 250% of the federal poverty level that installs insulation, air sealing and other energy-saving measures.
How much is the Charge Up incentive?
$1,500 for a new electric car, or $4,000 for income-qualified buyers who pre-qualify, plus up to $250 for a home charger.
Does the state pay for heat pumps?
Not directly. The utilities pay for heat pumps. The state's federal-funded rebates have no launch we could find.
No cash rebate, but there are solar credits of $77 per megawatt-hour and net metering.
